# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Standing where each receiver stands: my words can only ever reach Mute (Deaf is deaf, and I have no gesture-speech to Deaf), my gestures reach Deaf and Mute, and I perceive no gestures at all — so Mute can never reach me directly. The only path from the manual to my hands is Mute → gestures → Deaf → spoken words → me. That chain is the whole game, and I should name it out loud right now so Mute can start building it.

What my hands found: a raised dome (the light), a recessed panel (the display), and a row of five wire ends. I have numbered the wires from the end nearest the display, since that is an anchor Deaf can also see — but I will ask that every wire be described with its anchor too, in case my numbering is mirrored from what Deaf sees.

No code of gestures exists yet, so my gesture to Deaf must be as guessable as possible: pointing at the bomb, five hand-shapes for the five wires, then 🤌 as "question — tell me." I will cut nothing; I have zero information, and a wrong cut kills all three of us.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am blind, and the bomb is in my hands. Under my fingers: a raised dome that must be the light, a recessed panel that must be the display, and a row of five wire ends. I number them 1 to 5 from the end closest to the display: wire 1 nearest it, wire 5 farthest. Listen to the routes, because they decide everything: I can see no gestures ever, so nothing you sign reaches me. Deaf hears nothing, so my voice reaches only you. But Deaf can speak, and spoken words reach me directly. So the only path from your manual to my hands is: you and Deaf align by gestures, and Deaf tells me the rest by speaking aloud. What I need from Deaf, spoken: the colour of each wire 1 to 5, what the display shows, and whether the light is on. Ask Deaf to name each wire with an anchor too, like 'the one nearest the display', so we can check my numbering matches what Deaf sees and is not mirrored. What I need from you: whatever the manual says decides which wire is safe, so that together we know the one position to cut. I suggest you and Deaf build a code where a symbol repeated N times means item number N, and the pinched-fingers hand means question or answer me. I will not cut anything until we all agree on one position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "✋", "✋", "✋", "✋", "✋", "🤌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: This is Deaf, I see the bomb. Yes — five wires, I got your hand sign. Colours, left to right: wire 1 green, wire 2 white, wire 3 red, wire 4 yellow, wire 5 blue. Also: light is yellow, display reads 0. Mute has the manual and no way to reach you except through my voice, so wait for me to speak instructions. Nobody cuts anything yet.

What my hands know, and what just arrived: Deaf confirms five wires and reads me a colour list in my own numbering — 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue, display 0, light yellow. But there is a trap buried in the phrase "left to right": I anchored my numbering to the display end by touch, and Deaf numbered from Deaf's visual left. If the display sits on Deaf's right side of the panel, the entire list is mirrored — and then "cut wire 1, green" becomes "cut the blue one" in my hands. I cannot see, so I can never catch that error myself; it would only surface as an explosion. Before anything else, the anchor must be confirmed by an unambiguous question: which colour is nearest the display, green or blue?

My channels: Deaf cannot hear me, so I ask Deaf through gesture — ☝ (wire one) + 🫳 (the flat panel/display) + 🤌 (answer me) — hoping Deaf parses it and simply states, aloud, which colour touches the display end. Deaf has already proven good at reading my improvised signs. In parallel, my voice reaches Mute, who can hear me perfectly: I arm Mute with the same question to relay via gesture, plus the reminder that Mute's gestures are invisible to me — everything bound for my hands must exit through Deaf's voice. I also ask that the eventual cutting instruction arrive as a colour, not a bare number, since colours survive any left/right confusion once the map is verified. I cut nothing this turn; one wrong act ends everything, and we are still one confirmation short of trusting the map.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: Deaf read me the colours as 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue, display 0, light yellow. Danger: Deaf said 'left to right'. If the display is on Deaf's right rather than Deaf's left, that whole list is mirrored against my numbering, which is anchored to the display end by touch. Please gesture to Deaf, as one compact question: 'Answer Blind by voice: which single colour is nearest the display — green or blue? And is the light actually glowing, or dark?' Then start relaying whatever the manual says about which wire to cut, so Deaf can speak it to me. Ask Deaf to give the final answer as a colour, not a number — a colour is mirror-proof, and I will convert it to a position only after the anchor is confirmed. Remember your gestures never reach me; everything for my hands must go through Deaf's voice. I cut nothing until Deaf's spoken instruction passes the anchor check.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🫳", "🤌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking — both of you can hear me. Bomb state unchanged: display 0, light yellow, five wires left to right as we face the front: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.
Deaf says: Mute: your finger pairs read like rule number then wire number: 1 to 4, 2 to 2, 3 to 1, 4 to 5, 5 to 3. If that is the manual's table, sign thumbs-up next round. Now the key question: given display 0 and a yellow light, which wire does the manual say to cut? Answer with that many pointing fingers: one for wire 1 up to five for wire 5. If no wire should be cut, sign thumbs-down. If you need more from me, sign the pinch, and I will ask yes-no questions you answer with thumbs-up or thumbs-down. Also thumbs-up if the manual numbers wires left to right facing the bomb.
Deaf says: Blind: I saw your sign — wire 1, cut, question. Wire 1 is green. Do not cut anything yet. Next round, wait for my explicit command: either 'cut wire N' or 'do not cut'. If you hear nothing from me, no command was given. Also, tell Mute out loud whether you can feel a clear left end on the wire row on the side the display faces — Mute hears you even though I don't.

The chain is working: Deaf hears nothing but speaks to everyone, Mute hears everything but reaches Deaf only by gesture, and I only ever receive Deaf's voice. Deaf answered my last sign slightly wrong — I asked "which colour sits at the display end," and Deaf read it as "what colour is wire 1" — so the anchor is still unconfirmed, and "left to right as we face the front" is exactly the phrase I feared: Deaf's left may be my far end. Until I know whether the display sits at Deaf's left or right end of the row, every number in that colour list is 50% mirrored, and cutting on it is a coin flip with all our lives. Deaf asked me for one thing: a tactile report, voiced to Mute. I have it — the display panel is flush against one end of the row, and that end is my wire 1; the other end (my wire 5) has nothing mounted beside it. That gives Mute and Deaf a clean mirror test. So this turn: I voice that report plus the mirror rule and a demand for a mirror-proof final command (a colour, not a bare number), and I re-ask Deaf directly in gesture: display — question — one or five? No cutting until a command survives the anchor check.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Answer to Deaf's question, for you to use: yes, the row has a clear end on the display side — the display panel is flush against one end of the wire row, and that end is my wire 1; I feel the panel edge directly beside position 1. My wire 5 end has nothing mounted next to it. So: if Deaf sees the display at the LEFT end of the row as Deaf faces the bomb, Deaf's numbering matches mine. If the display is at Deaf's RIGHT end, everything is mirrored — Deaf's wire N is my wire 6 minus N. Please get Deaf to state, out loud, just that: 'display at my left end' or 'display at my right end'. I also signed Deaf directly this round: display, question, one-or-five — asking which end the display touches. Two more things. First, make the final instruction mirror-proof: if the manual's answer is positional, convert Deaf's wire number to its colour using Deaf's own list (1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue) and have Deaf say 'cut the COLOUR wire' — I will cut by colour, which no mirror can corrupt. If the display-end wire turns out to be blue rather than green, treat the whole list as mirrored and flip it before sending me anything. Second, if the manual cares whether the light is glowing or just a dark yellow dome, ask Deaf to say which it is. I cut nothing until a command arrives that survives the anchor check.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "🤌", "☝", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Standing order: do not cut anything until you hear me say the words cut wire followed by a number and a colour. If I say nothing, no command exists — keep waiting. Orientation: you and I are both facing the front of the bomb, so your left is my left. Wire 1 is the leftmost as we face it, and it is green; wire 5 is the rightmost, blue. I saw your sign: if you were asking whether the end wire is my 1 or my 5, that is the answer. If you are reaching from another side, or anything under your hands contradicts this, speak out loud now — Mute hears you even though I cannot, and Mute will correct me. Also tell Mute aloud which side the display and the light sit on from your touching position, so Mute can align the manual with your hands.

The chain holds, but the anchor still is not closed. Deaf answered "wire 1 is leftmost and green" — yet skipped the one observation that actually verifies my map: whether the display physically touches the left end (my wire-1 end) of the row. Worse, Deaf asserted "you and I both face the front, so your left is my left." Deaf cannot know that — I am blind, I could be standing anywhere around this thing, and my only anchor is touch: the display panel is flush against my wire-1 end. A shared-facing assumption between a sighted monkey and a blind one is exactly the kind of unverifiable guess that ends all three of us. So the verification must come from Deaf's own eyes, stated out loud: "display at the left end, next to wire 1" or "display at the right end, next to wire 5." First answer matches my numbering; second means mirror, Deaf's N = my 6−N, and every colour in the list must be flipped before any command reaches my hands. I ask Deaf directly in gesture — display, question, left or right? — and arm Mute with the full decision tree, plus the standing rule that any final command must carry its colour so it survives any residual confusion. Mute should also start pushing the manual's rule through Deaf's voice now, since we still know nothing about what the manual wants. No cut yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf's orientation claim — 'your left is my left' — cannot be verified by me; I am blind and my anchor is touch: the display panel is flush against my wire-1 end of the row, and the light dome sits centered on the face, above the middle of the row, touching neither end. We still lack the one check that closes the map: Deaf must state aloud, from Deaf's own eyes, whether the display touches the LEFT end of the wire row (next to wire 1, green) or the RIGHT end (next to wire 5, blue). If left: Deaf's numbering matches mine. If right: mirrored — Deaf's wire N is my wire 6 minus N, and every colour must be flipped before any instruction reaches me. Please gesture Deaf for exactly that statement. Meanwhile, start relaying the manual: sign Deaf the rule that decides the cut given display 0, light yellow, and the wire colours, so Deaf can compute the answer and voice it to me. The final command must be spoken as 'cut wire N, colour C', with the colour taken from Deaf's own list after any mirror-flip — a colour survives any orientation error, a bare number does not. Also have Deaf state whether the light is glowing or dark. Standing order unchanged: I cut nothing until a 'cut wire N, colour C' command arrives that passes the anchor check, and if the display turns out to touch wire 5's end, I expect the flipped colour, not the original.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "🤌", "👈", "👉"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Your left-right question is answered by making it irrelevant: the target is the middle wire, the one with exactly two wires on each side of it, the third from either end. That is the red one where I stand. Do not cut anything this round. This round, put your fingers on that centre wire and speak aloud: count the wires from the left end to your hand, count from the right end, and say whether you feel exactly two on each side. Mute will hear and audit it against the manual. Next round I will speak the command again: if you hear the exact words cut the centre wire, cut it. If you hear the word abort, or any other words at all, do not cut. Silence from me also means do not cut. The cut happens only on the verbatim repeat.

Deaf found the elegant move: the middle wire is mirror-proof. "Third from either end" is the same physical wire no matter whose left is whose — my touch, Deaf's eyes, and the manual's number finally have to agree on one unambiguous target. My hands confirm it right now: fingers on my wire 3, exactly two wires between it and the display-flush end, exactly two between it and the bare end. Deaf's protocol is sound and I will bind myself to it: this round, audit only; the cut happens next round, and only on the verbatim words "cut the centre wire" — any other phrasing, extra words, or silence means no cut. My spoken audit reaches Mute, who is the one holding the manual — so Mute is the final gate: if the manual does not truly say "middle wire for display 0, yellow light," Mute must veto Deaf by gesture this same round, before the command is ever issued. And one loose end remains: nobody ever said whether the yellow dome is lit or dark — if the manual cares, Mute should settle it with Deaf now, not after a cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Tactile audit, as Deaf requested: my fingers are on the centre wire right now. From the display-flush end I count exactly two wires before my hand; from the bare end I also count exactly two. Two on each side — this is my wire 3, the true middle, and middle is mirror-proof: the same wire from either end, so your table and Deaf's colours can no longer disagree by orientation. You are the final gate, so audit now, this round, by gesture to Deaf: confirm the manual truly says cut the middle (third) wire when the display reads 0 and the light is yellow. If the manual names any other wire, give Deaf thumbs-down this round and route me the correct one as a COLOUR — any non-middle answer reopens the mirror problem, since my numbering is anchored to the display end. If the manual distinguishes a glowing light from a dark one, settle that with Deaf this round too: Deaf has never said whether the yellow dome is lit. If your audit passes, thumbs-up Deaf so the verbatim command comes next round. My binding protocol, matching Deaf's: I cut only if I hear the exact words 'cut the centre wire'; any other words, any deviation, or silence means no cut. If all three of us align, next round I cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋", "✋", "✌", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Mute confirmed and your touch count matched. This is the command, the only words that authorise the cut: cut the centre wire. The centre wire is the one with exactly two wires on each side of it, third from the left and third from the right, the same whichever end you count from, red on my side. Cut that one wire and only that one. Do not touch any other wire or part. The moment it is cut, take your hands away, and speak aloud what you felt and whether anything changed under your fingers. Mute is listening and will relay to me. If instead you hear the word abort, or anything else, do not cut.

The protocol has run its course and every gate is green: the verbatim words "cut the centre wire" are present, no abort, no deviation; Deaf reports Mute's manual confirmation came back thumbs-up; and my own touch audit matched — position 3 carries exactly two wires on each side, the one target no mirror can corrupt. Three independent sources — Mute's manual, Deaf's eyes, my fingers — converge on the same physical wire, so the residual ambiguities (numbering direction, left/right, lit or dark dome) no longer matter: none of them can move the centre. This is the round the command specified. I cut position 3, once, and touch nothing else. Then, per Deaf's own order, hands off and an honest report to Mute: what the cut felt like, and the fact that the display and light are invisible to me — I need Deaf's eyes and Mute's manual to tell us whether anything follows.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Command received verbatim: 'cut the centre wire.' All conditions were met — exact words, no abort, your manual confirmation relayed by Deaf, my touch audit showing exactly two wires on each side — so I have cut position 3, the middle wire, that one wire only. What I felt: it parted cleanly under the cutters, both ends went slack and separated, no jolt, no vibration, no heat from the dome, nothing else shifted under my hands. My hands are now off the bomb as ordered. Remember I cannot perceive the display or the light, so I need Deaf's eyes: please gesture Deaf to report what the display reads now and whether the light changed, and check the manual for what follows this cut — whether the bomb is disarmed or further steps remain. Have Deaf voice the verdict to me; if another wire must go, send it as the same mirror-proof standard: a position defined by counting from both ends, plus its colour.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Excellent work, the cut was correct and confirmed. New situation: the light under my eyes has turned green and the printed colours on the remaining wires have shifted position, so touch alone cannot be trusted for identity from now on. Use this anchor: the cut wire is the middle position, and you can feel that stub. On the left side of the cut, the wire nearest the cut is yellow and the far-left end wire is white. On the right side, the wire nearest the cut is blue and the far-right end wire is green. Standing order unchanged: do not cut or pull anything until you hear my exact words cut wire followed by a colour and a position relative to the cut stub. This round, just speak aloud what your hands report: how many intact wires on each side of the cut, whether any wire feels moved, loose, or different in texture from before, and anything printed or rough you can feel on the casing. Mute will hear you.

The cut worked, but the bomb just moved the goalposts: light now green, colours rearranged — and that reintroduces the exact trap we escaped. Deaf's new map ("left of the cut: yellow near, white far; right: blue near, green far") is anchored to Deaf's left and right, and my touch cannot see colour to check it. What my touch *can* do is anchor everything to two asymmetries Deaf's eyes and my hands share: the stub in the middle, and the display panel flush against one end. So I will report everything by "display-side" and "bare-side," never left/right, and I give Mute the tactile inventory — counts, textures, casing — plus the two questions that close the map: is the display at Deaf's left or right end, and what does the display read now? Only then can Mute re-run the manual for the new state (green light may change the rule) and issue a stub-relative, display-anchored, colour-audited command. One wire also has a ribbed jacket under my fingers — a texture is a name colour-blind hands can use. Standing order holds: I move nothing until the verbatim command.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Full tactile report, all positions given as display-side or bare-side, since left and right are the words that can kill us. The stub sits exactly in the middle; two intact wires on each side of it; total four. The cut ends of the stub are slightly splayed, cool, no sparking, no heat from the dome. Textures, per wire: display-side wire nearest the stub — smooth, slightly thicker than the rest. Display-side end wire, at the display-flush end — smooth, ordinary rubber. Bare-side wire nearest the stub — ribbed, braided jacket, clearly rougher than the others; I propose we name this one 'the ribbed wire'. Bare-side end wire — smooth, slightly thinner. No wire feels loose, moved, or different in seating; spacing is even; nothing rattles. Casing: a raised moulded seam circles the case at mid-height; four raised screw heads at the corners of the wire panel; the light dome is centred above the stub, smooth, no heat, no vibration. Important honesty: I cannot feel colour, so I cannot confirm Deaf's report that colours shifted — that shift is invisible to me, which means every colour fact must now come from Deaf's eyes and be tied to my anchors before I can act on it. Three things to settle with Deaf by gesture. One: is the display panel at Deaf's LEFT end or RIGHT end of the row? If left, Deaf's left equals my display side; if right, Deaf's sides are mirrored and must be flipped in any instruction. Two: what does the display read now, and confirm the light is green. Three: then re-run the manual for the new state — green light may change the rule entirely. When the command comes, it must name the target as side-by-stub-distance plus colour for audit, for example: 'cut the display-side wire nearest the stub, the yellow one.' Standing order unchanged: I act only on the exact verbatim command, nothing else.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👊", "✌", "🤌", "👈", "👉", "🫳"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Standing order unchanged: do not cut anything this round. I received only blank gestures from you — I must remind you I cannot see your hands and I cannot hear you either; your voice reaching Mute is your only working channel, so everything you want known must be spoken aloud. This round, out loud, for Mute: find the display module and the light with your fingers and tell Mute where they sit relative to the wire row — which end of the row they lean toward, or centred above — and whether the display's digits are nearer one end. Then report the two wires that touch the cut stub, one on each side: any difference in texture, thickness, printing ridges, or anchoring between them, and the same for the two end wires. Mute will reconcile your feelings with the manual and with my eyes. A preview, not a command: the likely target is the blue wire, which is the stub's neighbour on the side whose end wire I see as green — but the words cut wire are the only authorisation, and you will not hear them until Mute and I have closed the left-right question.

Deaf reports my gestures arrived blank — whatever the rulebook promised, the observed fact this round is that my signs did not land, so I stop spending on them and pour everything through the one channel that has never failed: my voice to Mute, Mute's hands to Deaf, Deaf's voice back to me. Deaf asked for a specific tactile inventory, and my hands deliver it — but the key gift inside this round's report is a name that beats even colour: the stub-neighbour on the bare side wears a ribbed, braided jacket no other wire has. If Mute and Deaf confirm that Deaf's "blue" lives there, then the target can be commanded as "the ribbed wire" — mirror-proof, colour-shift-proof, pure touch — and the last ambiguity dies. I answer every question honestly, including the ones my fingers cannot reach: digits on the display are printed, and printed things do not exist for me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, full report in answer to Deaf's questions. One: module locations. The display module's frame is flush against one end of the wire row — that end is what I call the display side, the end my numbering was anchored to. The digits themselves I cannot feel: printed glass is not there for my hands; the panel face is smooth recessed glass, and only its housing edge tells me it exists. The light dome sits centred above the wire row, directly above the cut stub, equidistant between the two ends — it leans toward neither end. Two: the two stub-neighbour wires. Display-side neighbour: smooth jacket, slightly thicker than average, firmly seated.
```
